title: feature: wire model intelligence tiers to LiteLLM auto_router (not client heuristic)
description:
## Problem
lp-uxy.8 shipped Auto/Simple/Moderate/Complex in the composer with:
- **client-side heuristic** classifyMessageComplexity
- **global** patchSettingsActiveModel (settings.set active model)

LiteLLM already supports **Auto Routing** (complexity_router): config model groups SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/REASONING, heuristic or LLM classifier, call a single model id like `smart-router` / `auto_router/complexity_router`. Docs: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/auto_routing

Our deploy seed `deploy/litellm/config.yaml` is multi-provider model_list only — **no** auto_router tier groups.

## Goal
Model intelligence dropdown should route via **LiteLLM**, not reimplement routing in Portal.

## Design sketch
1. Add LiteLLM config entries for tier models + optional `lanyard-intelligence-router` with complexity_router_config tiers mapped Simple/Moderate/Complex (+ optional Reasoning)
2. Portal Auto → request model = router model id (per-request preferred; until host supports per-request, set_active to router id once)
3. Manual Simple/Moderate/Complex → set model to that tier group / pinned model name in LiteLLM
4. Remove or demote client heuristic to fallback only when LiteLLM router unavailable
5. Host agent must call LiteLLM with the selected model id (already via active model)
6. Document operator mapping: which real models back each tier

## Costs
- Auto LLM classifier: +cheap model call if classifier_type: llm (optional; default heuristic is free)
- Using Complex tier more often: higher model spend

## Related
- ADR 0007 (update or supersede routing section)
- deploy/litellm/config.yaml, README
- lp-uxy.8 selector UI (keep UX; change backend routing)
design:
LiteLLM proxy auto_router example (from docs):
  model_name: lanyard-auto
  litellm_params:
    model: auto_router/complexity_router
    complexity_router_config:
      tiers:
        SIMPLE: <cheap>
        MEDIUM: <mid>
        COMPLEX: <strong>
        REASONING: <optional>
    complexity_router_default_model: <mid>

Portal mapping:
  auto → lanyard-auto (or host alias)
  simple → SIMPLE pin model
  moderate → MEDIUM pin
  complex → COMPLEX pin

Prefer per-request model on chat inbound when available; until then set_active(router_or_tier_model).
acceptance_criteria:
- deploy/litellm (or host pin) defines tier models + auto_router model name for intelligence routing
- Composer Auto sends traffic through LiteLLM auto_router model id (not client-only tier pick + unrelated active model)
- Manual Simple/Moderate/Complex select the corresponding LiteLLM model_group / model_name
- Client heuristic either removed or documented fallback when router offline
- Smoke: litellm config validates; unit or integration proves model id mapping
- ADR 0007 amended or new ADR for LiteLLM-native path

Implemented on beads/lp-uxy.12-litellm-auto-router-intelligence

title: Chat agent tool: parse_document via Firecrawl AnyDoc (office/PDF → Markdown)
description:
## Why
Users attach PDFs/Office files (or agents fetch non-text docs from the web). Portal only stamps staging/vault **paths** into chat; soft-open is human preview, not model-ingest. Binary/non-text docs need conversion to Markdown/text so the model can reason over them.

## Product
Integrate **Firecrawl AnyDoc** (https://github.com/firecrawl/anydoc) — local Rust library (`@firecrawl/anydoc` / `firecrawl-anydoc`) that converts Word, PowerPoint, Excel, ODF, RTF, EPUB, CSV, and text PDFs to GFM Markdown (~single-digit ms, MIT). **Not Firebase.** Distinct from Firecrawl crawl/search (`lp-uxy.7`).

Scanned/image-only PDFs: anydoc returns unsupported → optional escalation to **Firecrawl Parse** hosted OCR (paid; cost-gated).

## Placement (decision)
**Primary: host agent tool** (`parse_document` / `extract_document_text`) on Hermes-Lanyard and Lanyard Agent.
**Portal:** label mapping + tool_progress UI only (no BFF-side parse of customer docs).
**Not BFF-only** — secrets and document bytes belong on the agent host plane (ADR 0002 external backends).

## Architecture sketch
```
User attach report.pdf
  → POST /api/staging/upload → /staging/uploads/.../report.pdf
User send
  → BFF appends [staging uploads] paths (message_type=document)
Agent turn
  → tool_progress running  parse_document  tool_target=path
  → host: anydoc.to_markdown_bytes (local) OR Firecrawl Parse OCR if scanned + key
  → tool_progress complete  result=Markdown (truncated) + optional .parse.md sidecar
  → model uses extracted text
```

## Costs
| Path | Cost |
|------|------|
| Local anydoc (office + text PDF) | **$0 SaaS** — library CPU on host; native deps/wheels |
| Firecrawl Parse OCR (scanned) | **Paid API** — only if FIRECRAWL_API_KEY set + policy allows |
| Portal UI labels | $0 |

## Related
- Epic lp-uxy; search/scrape: lp-uxy.7
- Upload: portal ChatView + BFF staging
- Soft-open ≠ ingest: portal-document-session-domain-model.md
- focr pack is offline ingest; chat still needs turn-time tool
- Tool events: portal-chat-tool-events.md, hermes-lanyard-tool-citations-contract.md

## Playbook
pstack **Feature** playbook (see design field). Track execution via child step beads.
design:
## Placement verdict
Agent tool on host (HL + LA). Portal transport + human labels only.
Principles that drove this: boundary-discipline (parse at agent host, not BFF);
model-the-domain (parse_document as explicit tool, not soft-open side effect);
experience-first (attach PDF → ask about it works without user knowing converter name).

## Data shape (name first)
```ts
// Host tool
type ParseDocumentArgs = {
  path: string;           // vault or /staging/uploads/... absolute
  max_chars?: number;     // default e.g. 48_000
  force_ocr?: boolean;    // optional cloud OCR path
  write_sidecar?: boolean;// default true → <stem>.parse.md next to source when writable
};

type ParseDocumentResult = {
  markdown: string;       // truncated body for tool result
  format: string;         // docx|pdf|...
  parser: "anydoc" | "firecrawl_parse" | "pdftotext" | "focr";
  chars: number;
  truncated: boolean;
  sidecar_path?: string;
  error_code?: "unsupported_scanned" | "path_denied" | "too_large" | "no_ocr_key";
};
```

## Pstack Feature playbook steps (execution beads)

### F0 — How / blast radius (read)
- Read portal-chat-tool-events, staging upload path, focr doctrine, anydoc README.
- Confirm agent can read staging paths on pilot pin (or file residual).

### F1 — Throughput checkpoint
- Ship HL tool first with local anydoc; Portal labels in same monorepo PR if HL already emits.
- LA parity as sister task if HL lands first.
- Do not block on Firecrawl Parse OCR v1.

### F2 — Architect types + module ownership
- HL/LA: tools/parse_document (or skills pack wrapper)
- Monorepo Portal: humanToolActivityLabel + CONTEXT_GATHERING
- Deploy: optional FIRECRAWL_API_KEY slot + approved processor for OCR only
- client-core: optional skill doc pointing agents to parse_document

### F3 — Implement host tool (local anydoc)
- Install firecrawl-anydoc or @firecrawl/anydoc on agent image / gateway env.
- path ACL under vault/staging; refuse escape.
- to_markdown / to_markdown_bytes; content-based format detection.
- Truncate + write sidecar when write_sidecar.
- Dual-emit tool_progress running/complete/error.

### F4 — Portal labels
- Map parse_document / extract_document_text → "Parsing a document"
- Prefer host tool_label when present.
- Unit tests on chatToolCallMapper / humanToolActivityLabel.

### F5 — Scanned PDF escalation (optional, cost-gated)
- On anydoc unsupported → if force_ocr or auto_policy + FIRECRAWL_API_KEY → Firecrawl Parse API.
- Fail closed with clear error when no key / processor not approved.
- Never put key on BFF.

### F6 — Prove it works
- Attach sample.docx + text PDF in chat; assert tool row + model cites content.
- Story or mocklab UI QA screenshots under artifacts/ui/lp-uxy.*/
- Negative: path outside tree denied; scanned PDF without key errors cleanly.

### F7 — Open PR(s)
- Monorepo PR: labels + docs + secrets docs.
- External HL/LA PR: tool implementation + pin bump notes.

## Non-goals
- Replacing document pane soft-open.
- Parsing on Portal BFF for every upload pre-send (optional future UX).
- Building a second OCR stack when focr exists for offline workers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Host tool parse_document (or documented alias) available on the pilot backend pin
- Dual-emits tool_progress running→complete/error with tool_target path; history retains row
- Local anydoc converts at least: .docx, .pptx or .xlsx, text .pdf → Markdown usable in model context
- Portal shows friendly activity label "Parsing a document" (or host tool_label)
- Staging upload path works end-to-end: attach → send → parse → answer uses text (proof)
- Path ACL: refuse paths outside vault/staging roots
- Scanned PDF: either OCR via cost-gated Firecrawl Parse OR clear unsupported error (no silent empty)
- FIRECRAWL_API_KEY only on host secrets envelope when OCR enabled; never BFF; never committed
- Costs documented: local free; OCR paid
- Evidence: docs note + QA artifacts/ui + pin/version when shipped
notes:
Source: https://github.com/firecrawl/anydoc (MIT). User said Firebase/AnyCrawl; product is Firecrawl AnyDoc. Related lp-uxy.7 is web search/scrape not office parse. Playbook: pstack Feature.

title: Composer model intelligence selector + LLM-as-judge auto routing
description:
## Problem
Users want model intelligence control always visible in the chat box bottom-right next to send: three tiers (complex / moderate / simple) plus Auto. Auto uses an LLM-as-judge (or classifier) to route. Today only Settings → Models active model exists; composer has project chip + attach + send. Message stamps active model for display only.

## Design sketch
1. UI: dropdown next to send — Auto | Simple | Moderate | Complex (labels TBD: Fast/Balanced/Smart)
2. Manual selection maps to configured model ids (Settings or deploy/litellm/config.yaml tiers)
3. Auto: light judge/classifier on user turn → tier → model for that request (or models.set_active if host only supports global active)
4. Persist last selection per user/thread
5. Capability-gate when model_selector unsupported

## Work
1. ADR: per-message model vs global active model (host API may need per-request model field)
2. Portal composer control + stamp/routing
3. Backend: tier map + optional judge step (cheap model); never block send if judge fails (fallback default)
4. Do not reuse self-improve nightly judge without redesign (different purpose)
5. Settings can still manage which models back each tier

## Related
deploy/litellm; config.schema auxiliary; model_selector affordance
acceptance_criteria:
- Dropdown visible bottom-right near send with three tiers + Auto
- Manual tier routes subsequent sends to the mapped model
- Auto routes without manual pick; selection indicator shows Auto and effective tier when known
- Settings unsupported → control hidden or disabled with clear state

title: Agent sandbox: cwd path ACL proof + Omnibox Mode A product wrap
description:
## Research answer
Sandboxing is layered, host-enforced. Portal only stamps working_directory / chat_topic. Without host path ACL and with admin shell_exec + Omnibox off, agents can run commands and scripts outside the project working directory. Omnibox Mode A (bubblewrap for tool children) is deploy-ready but default OFF and product must wrap shell_exec. Daytona VM isolation is separate epic lp-kng.

## Work
1. Live negative probes: file tools + shell attempt path escape; document pass/fail on HL and LA pins
2. Complete Omnibox product hook so OMNIBOX_ENABLED=1 actually prefixes host-impacting tools (deploy/references/omnibox-mode-a-hermes-hook.md)
3. Mocklab host.sandbox_enforced becomes live evidence where possible (not unit-only residual)
4. Document residual: shared kernel, admin blast radius; link lp-kng for VM isolation
5. Optional: default deny shell for Portal sessions unless operator opts in

## Related
lp-kng Daytona; docs/security/lp-p37.6 headless fail-closed; threat-model-private-by-default

title: Complex multi-tool turns stall or LITELLM_TIMEOUT without final result
description:
User report: complex tool turns (web search, complex Excel, many sub-agents) show intermediate 'gathering/creating' then never deliver final results. Gateway logs show [LITELLM_TIMEOUT] LiteLLM request timed out on multi-minute turns.

Simpler single web search in QA sometimes completes with prose + URLs. Stress cases (10 sub-agents each with table+chart) fail.

Acceptance:
1. Diagnose timeout budget (model, tool loop, portal SSE idle) and document where stall occurs.
2. Agent/Portal surfaces timeout as clear error (not silent intermediate).
3. Long multi-tool runs either complete or fail closed with retryable message; no infinite intermediate-only state.
4. Optional: raise safe timeout for multi-tool turns; stream intermediate tool results to UI so user sees progress.
5. Repro notes for subagent fan-out and Excel create.

Evidence: ~/.lanyard-agent/logs/gateway-pilot.log LITELLM_TIMEOUT entries; user reports.
notes: LA commit 58f72c5 on beads/lp-95v.4-complex-tool-timeout: fail-closed user-facing timeout delivery + default 180s completion timeout + litellm.timeout_ms. Tests providers/config/gateway-core pass. Pilot needs gateway rebuild/restart. Summary /tmp/grok-1000/beads-execute-1785525986/summary-lp-95v.4.md
